title: 2020 AMC 10A 24
statement: Let \(n\) be the least positive integer greater than \(1000\) for which \[ \begin{gathered} \gcd(63,n+120)=21\\ \text{and}\\ \gcd(n+63,120)=60. \end{gathered} \] What is the sum of the digits of \(n?\)

solutions.text:
The first gcd condition gives \(n+120\equiv0\pmod{21}\), so \(n\equiv6\pmod{21}\), but \(n+120\) must not be divisible by \(63\). The second gives \(n+63\equiv0\pmod{60}\), so \(n\equiv57\pmod{60}\), but \(n+63\) must not be divisible by \(120\).

Solving \(n\equiv6\pmod{21}\) and \(n\equiv57\pmod{60}\) gives \(n\equiv237\pmod{420}\). The candidates above \(1000\) are \(1077,1497,1917,\ldots\). The first fails the first gcd condition, the second fails the second gcd condition, and \(1917\) works. The digit sum is \(18\). Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Translate each gcd condition into a congruence plus an exclusion
Solve the two congruences first, then test candidates above \(1000\)
